findings.evidence: Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/L2Space.lean:45 `theorem memLp_two_iff_integrable_sq_norm {f : α → F} ...` with `variable {α F : Type*} ... [NormedAddCommGroup F]` (line 40); Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/LpSeminorm/TriangleInequality.lean:175 `MemLp.sub`; Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Integral/Bochner/Basic.lean:770 `integral_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg {f : α → ℝ}`.
findings.fix: Split the section: state it as `theorem integral_norm_sub_integral_sq_eq_zero_iff {E} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hf : MemLp f 2 μ) : ∫ x, ‖f x - ∫ y, f y ∂μ‖ ^ 2 ∂μ = 0 ↔ f =ᵐ[μ] fun _ ↦ ∫ y, f y ∂μ`, keeping `[InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E]` only on `integral_norm_sub_integral_sq`. The existing proof script goes through unchanged.
findings.issue: `MemLp.integral_norm_sub_integral_sq_eq_zero_iff` inherits `[InnerProductSpace ℝ E]` from the section variables (line 44), but its proof uses no inner product: only `memLp_two_iff_integrable_sq_norm`, `MemLp.sub`, `memLp_const`, `integral_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg` and `sub_eq_zero`. The instance is kept alive only because `∫ y, f y ∂μ` needs a `NormedSpace ℝ E`, so the unused-section-variable linter cannot catch it. In a file explicitly written for upstreaming this is a strictly too-strong hypothesis.

findings.evidence: Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/LpSeminorm/Basic.lean:864 `MemLp.norm`; Mathlib/Probability/Moments/Variance.lean:204 `variance_nonneg`, :226 `variance_eq_sub [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {X : Ω → ℝ} (hX : MemLp X 2 μ) : variance X μ = μ[X ^ 2] - μ[X] ^ 2`; the definitions at Basic.lean:89-102 require only `[NormedSpace ℝ E]`.
findings.fix: Move both into the `Definitions` section with `[NormedSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E] [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (hA : MemLp A 2 μ)`, proving `coherentCrossSection_le_totalDiffractiveCrossSection` from `norm_integral_le_integral_norm` plus `variance_nonneg`/`variance_eq_sub` applied to `hA.norm`, and deriving `incoherentCrossSection_nonneg` from it by `sub_nonneg`.
findings.issue: `incoherentCrossSection_nonneg` and `coherentCrossSection_le_totalDiffractiveCrossSection` (line 180) sit in the `InnerProductSpace ℝ E` section, but both hold at the level the definitions themselves use (`[NormedSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E]`): `‖∫ A‖² ≤ (∫ ‖A‖)² ≤ ∫ ‖A‖²` by `norm_integral_le_integral_norm` and non-negativity of the real variance of `‖A‖`. Proving them only via the Good–Walker identity attaches a hypothesis the statements do not need.

summary: Two statements carry an inner-product hypothesis they do not need: the vanishing criterion in the upstream-namespace Variance file, and the two order facts in GoodWalker, all of which hold for any real normed space. Everything else sits at the natural level.
